title: Disable a kernel module
description: Disable a loadable Linux kernel module by blacklisting it, preventing it from loading, and unloading it if currently active.

playbook_input.description: Parameters the caller provides before execution

parameters.name: target_server
parameters.description: The target Linux host to SSH into (IP or hostname).

parameters.name: kernel_module_name
parameters.description: Name of the kernel module to disable (e.g. cramfs, udf).

playbook_output.description: Structured result of the module disable operation

fields.name: module_found
fields.description: True if the module was found as a loadable kernel object.

fields.name: loaded_before
fields.description: True if the module was loaded before the playbook ran.

fields.name: module_unloaded
fields.description: True if the module was successfully unloaded by this playbook.

fields.name: config_updated
fields.description: True if the modprobe.d configuration was created or modified.

steps.name: Set default not‑found output variables
steps.function: Initialize output facts to the 'module not found / no action needed' state so the emit step always has valid data. Also compute the modprobe.d configuration file path.

computations._status_message: Module not available or built‑in, no remediation necessary.

steps.name: Find kernel module files on disk
steps.function: Search /lib/modules for .ko files matching the target module name.

steps.name: Is the module available as a loadable kernel object?
steps.function: Branch on whether any .ko file was found for the target module.
steps.condition: The search for kernel module files returned at least one result.

steps.name: Ensure install /bin/false line in modprobe.d
steps.function: Write (if missing) the line 'install <module> /bin/false' into the module's .conf file under /etc/modprobe.d.

steps.name: Ensure blacklist line in modprobe.d
steps.function: Write (if missing) the line 'blacklist <module>' into the module's .conf file under /etc/modprobe.d.

steps.name: Check if the module is currently loaded
steps.function: Run lsmod and grep for the module name to determine if it is actively loaded in the kernel.

steps.name: Derive loaded flag from lsmod result
steps.function: Set _loaded_before to true if the grep exit code was 0 (module found in lsmod).

steps.name: Is the module currently loaded?
steps.function: Branch on whether the kernel module is currently loaded, to decide if an unload attempt is needed.
steps.condition: The kernel module is currently loaded.

steps.name: Unload the module (never fails)
steps.function: Run modprobe -r and rmmod to remove the module; errors are ignored and captured via return code.

steps.name: Assemble final output variables
steps.function: Update output facts with the actual results of configuration and unloading.

steps.name: Emit final result
steps.function: Print the structured result block containing module status and summary message.

steps.name: Abort on failure
steps.function: Reached via the playbook's rescue block on any task failure. Prints the required error output and fails the play.

phases.name: Pre‑checks and discovery
phases.description: Set default output facts and determine whether the target kernel module exists as a loadable object.

phases.name: Main remediation
phases.description: Ensure the module is blacklisted and optionally unload it if currently active.

phases.name: Result assembly
phases.description: Derive the final output variables from the remediation actions.

phases.name: Error handling
phases.description: Reached when any step fails; records failure and halts execution.
